To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of preganglioniic neurons forming connections with stellate ganglions in cats increased during the first 10 days after birth and then decreased, reaching a level that is comparable to that in adults by the age of six months.

the number of preganglioni cells innervating the stellate sympathetic ganglion increases during the first 10 days of postnatal life and then declines, and this is accompanied by changes in the distribution of these cells among the spinal cord nuclei.

during postnatal ontogeneis, the number of preganglioni neurons forming connections with stellate ganglia increased from birth to ten days of age and then decreased, the proportion of preganglional neurons in different spinal nuclei changed during life, and the number of neurons forming connections with this ganglion increased in the nucleus intermediomedialis thoracolumbar pars principalis with a decrease in nucleus intermediomedialis thorcolumbar pars funicularis and ventral horns of spinal cord.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ontogenesis of the preganglionic innervation of the stellate (postganglionic sympathetic) ganglion.
the development of the stellate preganglionic system during ontogenesis.
the ontogenetic development of the stellate preganglionic neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number and distribution of preganglionic sympathetic neurons in the stellate sympathetic ganglia of the cat change significantly during postnatal development.

the stellate sympathetic ganglia of the cat are innervated by preganglionic neurons located in the intermediolateral columns of the thoracic spinal cord, and that this innervation undergoes changes in the number of preganglional neurons and in the distribution of these neurons among spinal cord nuclei during postnatal development of the animal.
the number of neurons connected to the stellates ganglion is maximal during the first 10 days of life and then gradually declines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in cats the stellate sympathetic ganglion is supplied by preganglionic neurons located in the thoracic, lumbar and sacral spinal cord segments, and that this supply is not uniform during postnatal ontogenic development.
the number of preganglioni neurons and spinal cord nuclei connected to the stellates ganglion increase from birth to 20 days of age, after which the number decreases.
the stellate sympathetic ganglion receives inputs from the spinal cord during postnatal ontogeny, and the proportion of neurons in the different nuclei changes during life.

the number and proportion of preganglioni cells connected to the stellare ganglion changes during postnatal ontogeneis.
